extracted.intended_audience: experimental physicists, inventors, and scientifically literate readers interested in radiophony/spectroscopy (and secondary: forestry educators/administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, constructing, and measuring sonorous effects produced by radiant energy (radiophony), including instrument construction (spectrophonic/spectrophone), measurement methods, and material selection. Also contains historical/administrative standards for forestry schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum: cultivation and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivation and management of forests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an essential subject for forestry instruction (enumerated item 5 in the curriculum list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum: sub-forester practical information
rubrics_metrics.description: The information most important to sub-foresters concerning the working of forests, forest police and protection, and book-keeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly given as a curricular requirement (enumerated item 6), i.e., practical administrative and protection knowledge for sub-foresters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum class size
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of pupils shall not exceed thirty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hard administrative limit on enrollment for the (described) forestry institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant age and primary education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicants must be at least eighteen years of age, and must pass an examination in the primary studies as taught at the best schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission criterion; successful completion of the course leads to a certificate enabling appointment to manage forests under Confederation/cantonal control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher appointment and remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: The teachers of these institutes are appointed by the cantons, subject to the approval of the Federal authority, but they are paid from the general treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative standard for staffing and funding of forestry institutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: District forest school oversight and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: District forest schools are under the oversight of the Forest Bureau and each under the visitation of the forest inspector; each forest school is presided over by a president (teacher) with a forest overseer as assistant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational requirement: administrative oversight, dual-role presidency/teaching, and an assistant overseer; schools placed in public forests and subject to inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course duration and public examination (district schools)
rubrics_metrics.description: The course of instruction embraces one full year, at the end of which the pupils have a public examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized course length for district schools; public examination as completion requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher institutes: course length and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher forestry/agronomic institutes (e.g., Villaviciosa/San Lorenzo, St. Petersburg, Petrovsk, Lissino) have multi-year courses (commonly three years); admission to some requires prior gymnasium education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that professional schools for forest engineers/forestry sections run multi-year programs (often three years) and may require prior secondary schooling; graduates receive ranks/appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical instruction facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutes 'well furnished with grounds, cabinets, and collections adapted to give practical instruction' (example: General Institute of Agriculture at Lisbon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical resources and collections are a criterion for adequate practical instruction in forestry/agronomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purity of selenium for photonic sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Selenium samples were found to contain sulphur, iron, lead, and arsenic with traces of organic matter; when these impurities are eliminated the selenium appears more constant in its action and more sensitive to light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental standard: chemical purity of selenium must be controlled/verified because impurities materially affect reproducibility and sensitivity of light-induced electrical resistance effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative materials: tellurium and alloys
rubrics_metrics.description: Tellurium, like selenium, has its electrical resistance affected by light; alloys of selenium and tellurium of different proportions may possess intermediate electrical properties and can be sensitive to light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material-selection guideline: test tellurium and selenium–tellurium alloys for different resistance/sensitivity trade-offs; do not assume selenium alone is optimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lampblack (smoked film) cells as practical receivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Lampblack cells (silver-deposited glass with zigzag-scratched combs filled with smoked lampblack) yield loud musical tones when exposed to interrupted sunlight and can substitute for selenium/tellurium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumentation/design recommendation: lampblack is inexpensive and effective; construction details (interlocking comb electrodes, smoked film filling interstices) are given and spongy metals can produce similar effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing effect with induction coil
rubrics_metrics.description: The audible effect is much increased by placing the tellurium cell with the battery in the primary circuit of an induction-coil, and placing the telephone in the secondary circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circuit configuration guideline: using an induction coil with the sensitive cell in the primary and the telephone in the secondary amplifies the audible output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensitive cells for reproduction of articulate speech
rubrics_metrics.description: The sensitive cells can be employed for the reproduction of articulate speech, as well as for the production of musical sounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional requirement: design and arrangement of cells/circuits should allow not just tones but intelligible speech reproduction; indicates viability of telephonic reception with such cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative sonorous power: focal-distance method
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure relative sonorous power by focusing a beam with lenses and determining the distances from the focal point at which two substances emit sounds of equal intensity; move one receiver along a graduated support until the ear decides the sounds are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental method 1: apparatus uses two similar lenses, an interrupting disk, receivers in vessels communicating via equal-length flexible tubes to a common hearing tube; one receiver fixed, the other adjusted to equality — note relative positions to compute relative sonorous powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative sonorous power: interference (phase-opposition) method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an interrupter consisting of a continuously vibrating tuning-fork with opaque screens to produce an undulating beam; arrange two receivers so sonorous vibrations reach the common hearing tube in opposite phases producing silence when equal in intensity; move one receiver until complete silence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental method 2: interference-based comparison gives a sensitive criterion of equality (complete silence) and uses unequal-length flexible tubes to create opposite phases; record relative receiver positions when silence occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration by electrical comparison (rheostat method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the loudness of a light-produced musical tone with that of a similar pitch electrically produced; introduce a rheostat into the electrical circuit to measure the amount of resistance required to render the electrical sound equal in intensity to the light-produced sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental method 3: provides a quantitative electrical calibration of sonorous intensity by measuring equivalent resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential acoustic balance using undulatory currents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the tuning-fork is vibrated by an undulatory instead of an intermittent current, an electrically produced tone in one receiver might extinguish the light-produced tone in the other, allowing establishment of an acoustic balance by introducing sufficient resistance into the electric circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested experimental extension: use synchronized undulatory electrical excitation to directly counteract radiophonic-induced sound and balance intensities electrically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation principle: sounds correspond to absorbed rays
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of the rays that produce sonorous effects in different substances depends upon the nature of the substances that are exposed to the beam, and the sounds are in every case due to those rays of the spectrum that are absorbed by the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical/interpretive criterion: when mapping or interpreting results, correlate audible bands with absorption bands of the test substance; this underlies the spectrophonic method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrophonic/spectrophone instrument construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the eyepiece of a spectroscope and place sensitive substances in the focal point behind an opaque diaphragm slit; connect these substances to the ear by a hearing-tube to convert the instrument into a spectrophone (spectrophonic receiver).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumentation guideline: spectrophonic receiver enables detection of absorption bands (silent positions) especially in the ultra-red where the eye is ineffective; lampblack/peroxide-of-nitrogen-filled receivers recommended for broad-range audibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of filtering/absorbing media to probe spectral response
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpose filters (e.g., saturated alum solution, hard rubber sheet, ammonia–copper sulfate solution) in the beam path and observe changes in audible bands; filtering can reduce ultra-red audibility or suppress visible-region sounds, revealing transmitted/invisible bands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental diagnostic: use selective filters to identify which spectral regions produce sonorous effects for a given receiver material; examples and observed results are provided to illustrate expected changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material-dependent spectral maxima mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Different receiver substances (lampblack, red worsted, green silk, hard-rubber shavings, vapors like ether/iodine/peroxide of nitrogen, selenium cell) show maxima and limits of audibility at different spectral positions (e.g., lampblack max far into ultra-red; peroxide of nitrogen maximum in the blue; selenium maximum in the red).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical guideline: determine the material-specific range and peak of sonorous response experimentally; useful for selecting receiver material depending on the spectral region of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrophonic advantage in ultra-red
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrophone is a most reliable and convenient substitute for the thermopile in the investigation of absorption spectra in the ultra-red; the ear is invaluable beyond the red where the eye is useless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological recommendation: use spectrophonic techniques for ultra-red spectroscopy; lampblack in the receiver is effective for ultra-red detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: adopt 'radiophone' umbrella term
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt 'radiophone' as a general term signifying an apparatus for the production of sound by any form of radiant energy, limiting 'thermophone', 'photophone', and 'actinophone' to thermal, luminous, or actinic rays respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization recommendation: use consistent terminology to avoid misunderstandings about which portion of radiant energy is implicated in observed effects.
